Saudi Basic Industries Corp Appoints New Chief Strategy Officer Amid Growth Drive

Riyadh – Saudi Basic Industries Corp, one of the world’s leading chemical manufacturers, has announced the appointment of Fahad Al-Mutairi as Chief Strategy Officer, effective immediately. The move is part of the company’s efforts to expand its global footprint and enhance operational efficiency as demand for petrochemicals continues to evolve.

Al-Mutairi, who previously held senior leadership roles in the region’s energy and industrial sectors, brings two decades of experience in strategic planning and transformation initiatives. He will report directly to CEO Khalid Al-Shehri and will be responsible for shaping the long-term vision of the company, identifying new growth markets, and overseeing corporate development activities.

“Saudi Basic Industries Corp is entering a new phase of growth, and we are delighted to welcome Fahad Al-Mutairi to our executive team,” said Al-Shehri in a statement released on Sunday. “His expertise in global strategy and proven track record in driving large-scale transformation will be invaluable as we pursue our goals of innovation, sustainability, and international expansion.”

Industry analysts say the appointment comes at a pivotal time for Saudi Arabia’s chemicals sector, which is seeing increased competition and a push towards higher-value products. “Strategic leadership is critical as the sector seeks to diversify its portfolio and respond to changing market dynamics,” said Lina Hariri, a chemicals industry analyst at the Gulf Trade Forum. “Saudi Basic Industries Corp has demonstrated resilience in recent years, and this appointment signals its commitment to maintaining a leading position in the global market.”

According to figures from the Saudi Industrial Development Authority, the chemicals industry accounted for nearly 30% of the Kingdom’s non-oil exports in 2023, underscoring its significance to the national economy. The company has also announced a series of investments in advanced manufacturing and sustainability initiatives, including partnerships with local technology firms such as Desert Innovations Ltd and GreenChem Solutions.

In his remarks, Al-Mutairi expressed enthusiasm for his new role. “I am honored to join Saudi Basic Industries Corp at such an exciting juncture,” he said. “Together with the team, I look forward to building on the company’s impressive legacy and driving new opportunities for growth and value creation.”

Shares in Saudi Basic Industries Corp closed marginally higher on Sunday, reflecting positive investor sentiment following the announcement.
